author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only page, reachable by its address alone, lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it shown by first name then last name, all on one page.
acceptance_criteria: given the clinic's specialties, when the specialty page is opened, then every specialty is listed by its stored name on a single page
given a specialty held by veterinarians, when the specialty page is opened, then each holder is listed under it by first name then last name
given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the specialty page is opened, then that veterinarian appears nowhere on the page
given any other page of the system, when it is rendered, then it carries no link to the specialty page
edge case 3: a veterinarian holding several specialties appears under each of them
edge case 4: a specialty that no veterinarian holds is still listed, shown as held by none
edge case 5: the specialties, and the veterinarians under each, are presented in a stable order rather than an arbitrary one
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties (NG-2 unchanged, per intake decision 1)
Any navigation entry or link from another page to the specialty page (intake decision 2; a visible entry point may come as a follow-up request)
Pagination of the specialty page (intake request: all specialties render on one page)
Searching or filtering specialties or veterinarians (NG-9 unchanged)
notes: Owner absent; no pushback raised: the request conflicts with no recorded requirement or Non-Goals row (NG-2 covers write flows only; NG-9 covers search, not a listing; REQ-SYS-001 requires every page to carry navigation to owner search and the veterinarian directory, which the new page inherits, and does not require navigation to the new page). Reversible decisions taken at the narrowest reading, recorded as PRD Open Questions: (1) a specialty no veterinarian holds is listed and shown as held by none, reading 'lists every specialty' literally; (2) order is stable but its key is left to design, mirroring REQ-VET-001 edge case 1. The address is the owner's GET /specialties.html. REQ-LANG-002 binds: every new piece of page wording lands in all eleven supported message bundles; the existing bundle-sync test carries that check. No new ubiquitous-language term: the PRD uses only Specialty and Veterinarian. Seven owed test names; one primary surface (code).

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Read-only inverse view inside the existing vet package (system-design § Package Structure, § Contracts); no new module, no cross-package edge, no new dependency. Adjustments: four new Contracts rows (SpecialtyRepository, SpecialtyHolders, GroupHoldersBySpecialty, SpecialtyController) plus REQ-VET-003 on Vet, Specialty, VetRepository; a new § Scale and Load section with the specialty-page row. Placement per architecture-principles § Logic Placement: the inversion and the order are a decision spanning several objects, so they live in a domain service (static pure methods, no stereotype, Language Realization § Building Blocks), never in the controller (Pattern Catalog Web controller row; the recorded controller deviation does not extend to new rules). SpecialtyRepository mirrors the PetTypeRepository precedent of a repository per lookup type. A separate SpecialtyController keeps VetController single-surface (§ Naming: prefixed by the surface it serves). Covering symbols resolved by grep (IDE oracle not connected, weaker basis): Vet.getSpecialties, VetRepository.findAll() @Cacheable("vets"), Specialty extends NamedEntity with no equals override, PetTypeRepository.findPetTypes. Verdict minor: every pattern used is already defined in the briefs; no decision constrains later slices, so no ADR — the order key is one clause on the GroupHoldersBySpecialty row.
integration_points: Entry point GET /specialties.html (owner-named address): binds no request parameter and no form object, so no binding target exists; the existing locale-switch parameter stays with WebConfiguration. A future parameter would bind to a request-scoped value, never a persisted type.

SpecialtyController sequences: SpecialtyRepository.findAll() + VetRepository.findAll() (the cached unpaged read) -> GroupHoldersBySpecialty -> model -> view vets/specialtyList. It renders through the shared layout fragment and passes a menu key matching no menu item, so no navigation entry is highlighted or added (intake decision 2).

Double, domain service tests (GroupHoldersBySpecialtyTests): no boundary crossed; real Vet and Specialty instances built in the test, including two distinct Specialty instances sharing one id to pin identity matching (testing-principles § Mocking Policy: real implementations).

Double, repository boundary in SpecialtyControllerTests: hand-written in-memory implementations of SpecialtyRepository and VetRepository registered as beans through a test configuration under @WebMvcTest, driven by MockMvc (the sanctioned transport stand-in). A Mockito stub is not named and would be a finding (testing-principles § Mocking Policy: hand-write mocks).

Double, the cross-page no-link check (theOtherPagesShouldCarryNoLinkToTheSpecialtyPage): real repositories over the embedded H2 seed via a full application context driven by MockMvc; it renders each page reachable by GET and asserts no href to /specialties.html.

Message bundles: every new page wording (page heading, column headings, the held-by-none text) lands as a key in all eleven bundles; I18nPropertiesSyncTest already enforces REQ-LANG-002 (system-design § Contracts, the requirement with no contract).

patterns.description: repository per lookup type; SpecialtyRepository extends Repository<Specialty, Integer> (not JpaRepository) exposing one read method, least privilege per security-principles § Trust Boundaries
controller shape: constructor-injected repositories, model attributes, view name; minus pagination
SpecialtyHolders is an immutable record with List.copyOf; GroupHoldersBySpecialty is a plain class of static pure methods, named by action (§ Naming domain-services row)

risks.risk: Specialty inherits object identity (no equals override), and the specialties inside cached Vet instances are different objects from those SpecialtyRepository returns; grouping by reference silently empties every specialty
risks.mitigation: GroupHoldersBySpecialty matches by specialty id, as its Contracts row states; a test uses distinct instances sharing an id (architecture-principles § Domain Core: decision in the testable core)

risks.risk: Specialty page path scales with all specialties and all veterinarians, unpaged (system-design § Scale and Load, specialty-page row)
risks.mitigation: simplest readable form: two full reads and one in-memory grouping; sizes are unrecorded and treated as bounded

risks.risk: Order unstable across databases: specialty names are not unique in any vendor schema, and the vet findAll carries no ORDER BY
risks.mitigation: all ordering lives in GroupHoldersBySpecialty with an identity tie-break (specialties by name then id; holders by last name, first name, then id); the controller and repository impose none (system-design § Contracts, GroupHoldersBySpecialty row)

risks.risk: Stored veterinarian and specialty names are echoed into HTML
risks.mitigation: render with th:text only, never th:utext (system-design § Threat Model, cross-site scripting row)

risks.risk: Business rule drifting into the controller (grouping, the no-holder case, ordering)
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyController sequences and selects the view only (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog Web controller row; § Design Validation Checklist)

notes: Owner absent (intake owner_present false). No foundational signal trips: design doc, vocabulary, and the persistence and error-flow patterns this slice touches are recorded; Specialty and Veterinarian are existing ubiquitous-language terms; vet is an existing package. The PRD left the order key to design (Open Question 2); the recorded key is specialties by stored name, holders by last name then first name, identity as the tie-break in both. No design-doc-autofix records to audit. Brief follow-ups outside this agent's write scope, for the owner of docs/architecture-principles.md: once GroupHoldersBySpecialty lands, the Domain service row under Pattern Catalog § Available, not currently used and the Naming sentence saying the last two rows name concepts the codebase does not yet contain become stale. author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Surface widening (security-principles.md row 'Widening the exposed surface'): the change adds one endpoint, SpecialtyController.java `@GetMapping("/specialties.html")`, a read-only GET that takes no request parameter, path variable, or bound object (signature `String showSpecialtyList(Model model)`). It exposes specialty names and veterinarian first/last names to any caller. That data is already public on /vets.html and the /vets serialized route (VetController.java:44 `@GetMapping("/vets.html")`, :65 `@GetMapping({ "/vets" })`), so no new data class reaches the open baseline. No management exposure changes.

Injection into data access: SpecialtyRepository declares only the derived `List<Specialty> findAll()` under `@Transactional(readOnly = true)` with no `@Query` and no write method. No request-derived value reaches any query.

XSS: specialtyList.html renders stored names only through escaping `th:text` (`${specialtyHolders.specialty.name}`, `${holder.firstName + ' ' + holder.lastName}`). `grep -rn -F 'th:utext' src/main/resources/templates/vets/` returns nothing. The layout menu argument 'specialties' is a template literal, so the layout's `__${link}__` preprocessing (fragments/layout.html:31) receives no request text from this page.
Mass assignment and binding: the diff adds no @ModelAttribute, @RequestBody, or @InitBinder target, so no binder is exposed and no disallow list is needed.

Resource bounds: the page loads all specialties and all vets unpaged. PRD REQ-VET-003 requires this ('All specialties appear on one page'), and it matches the existing unpaged, @Cacheable("vets") VetRepository.findAll() already served on /vets. The grouping in GroupHoldersBySpecialty is a linear in-memory inversion and allocates nothing beyond that.

Removed or weakened checks: none. The diff modifies no existing Java or template file. The only modified non-doc files are the 10 message bundles, each gaining two plain-text keys (specialty, vetsBySpecialty) with no markup.

Secrets: no credential, token, key, or connection string appears in the diff (read in full via python3 scripts/changeset.py). Error handling, logging, file I/O, process execution, and deserialization paths are untouched.

Supply chain: build.gradle is unchanged (git status --short build.gradle returned empty) and the change adds no dependency. The resolved runtimeClasspath from ./gradlew dependencies shows spring-boot 4.1.2, spring-webmvc 7.0.10, jackson-databind 3.1.7, and thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE. No NVD match ran: the security brief already lists 'no dependency vulnerability scan' as a standing gap.
